props.gloss_en: Beit Shammai: not even a cooked dish [is exempted]
the mishnah: if they were sitting, each blesses for himself; if they reclined, one blesses for all
reading 1: Beit Shammai dispute the first clause -- for the tanna kama bread exempts appetizers and all the more so a cooked dish; Beit Shammai say bread does not exempt even a cooked dish
reading 2: Beit Shammai dispute the last clause -- appetizers do not exempt bread, but they do exempt a cooked dish; Beit Shammai say they do not exempt even a cooked dish
if they reclined -- yes [one blesses for all]; if they did not recline -- no
the baraita: ten walking on the road, even if all eat from one loaf, each blesses for himself; if they sat to eat, even if each eats from his own loaf, one blesses for all

questions.gloss_en: do Beit Shammai ('not even a cooked dish') dispute the mishnah's first clause (bread) or its last (appetizers)? It stands unresolved

supports.gloss_en: היו יושבין כל אחד ואחד כו׳ -- from the mishnah's wording 'if they reclined': reclining, yes; not reclining, no

objections.gloss_en: ורמינהו: עשרה שהיו הולכים בדרך... ישבו לאכול... אחד מברך לכולם -- קתני ישבו אף על פי שלא הסבו: the baraita has sitting suffice without reclining
